about.title: About
about.subtitle: Ondulab
paragraphs: Ondulab was born from fifteen years of experimentation within Réso-nance Numérique and LFO, Marseille's first fablab. This journey has forged a culture of prototyping, collaboration and openness, with a constant objective: making digital instruments truly accessible.
Over time, one thing becomes clear: accessibility requires ergonomics, simplicity and autonomy of use. An instrument must be usable without technical prerequisites.

The meeting with Devisubox marks a turning point: moving beyond the prototype to design a reliable and industrializable object. Sp3ctra embodies this shift: a complete instrument, designed for real use, allowing non-experts to appropriate complex digital tools.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know about Sp3ctra

questions.question: What are the application areas of Sp3ctra?
questions.answer: Sp3ctra is aimed at musicians, visual artists, teachers, researchers and engineers wishing to explore linear capture and spectral synthesis. The instrument can be used for sound creation, interactive installations, teaching sound physics, or developing innovative interfaces.

questions.question: Do I need technical skills to use Sp3ctra?
questions.answer: No. Sp3ctra was designed to be accessible without technical prerequisites. The interface allows immediate handling through gesture and tactile exploration. For advanced uses (programming, integration), an open-source SDK and complete documentation are available.

questions.question: Can I develop my own applications with Sp3ctra?
questions.answer: Yes. Sp3ctra comes with an open-source SDK including Python, C/C++ and Max/MSP libraries. You can access raw sensor data via Ethernet or USB to create your own processing algorithms.

questions.question: What is the system latency?
questions.answer: The data flow is stable at 1 KHz with latency below 5 ms, ensuring a real-time experience suitable for live performances and gestural interactions.

questions.question: How can I try Sp3ctra?
questions.answer: You can test the instrument at the Cité des Sciences et de l'Industrie (Paris) until March 2026 as part of the exhibition 'The music of photons'. For a personalized demonstration or quote, contact us via the form.
